audit_status.source_base: ChatGPT-authored Psalms completion draft using public-domain KJV as familiar alignment scaffold with curated Hebrew/textual overrides; full WLC/OSHB/source-witness audit pending
audit_status.review_note: Vindication, hostile opposition, light, truth, altar, and the Psalm 42 refrain.

verses.restored: Judge me, O God, and plead my cause against an wicked nation: O deliver me from the deceitful and unjust man.

familiar.text: Judge me, O God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation: O deliver me from the deceitful and unjust man.

notes.title: Psalms 42–43
notes.body: Psalm 43 continues Psalm 42’s language and refrain without a separate superscription. Many interpreters treat the two as one poem.

modern.text: Vindicate me, O God, and plead my case against an ungodly nation; deliver me from deceitful and unjust men.

original.text: שָׁפְטֵ֤נִי אֱלֹהִ֨ים וְרִ֘יבָ֤ה רִיבִ֗י מִגּ֥וֹי לֹא חָסִ֑יד מֵ֤אִישׁ מִרְמָ֖ה וְעַוְלָ֣ה תְפַלְּטֵֽנִי

verses.restored: For thou art the God of my strength: why dost thou cast me off? why go I mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?

familiar.text: For thou art the God of my strength: why dost thou cast me off? why go I mourning because of the oppression of the enemy?

modern.text: For You are the God of my refuge. Why have You rejected me? Why must I walk in sorrow because of the enemy’s oppression?

original.text: כִּֽי אַתָּ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י מָֽעוּזִּי֮ לָמָ֪ה זְנַ֫חְתָּ֥נִי לָֽמָּה קֹדֵ֥ר אֶתְהַלֵּ֗ךְ בְּלַ֣חַץ אוֹיֵֽב

verses.restored: O send out thy light and thy truth: let them lead me; let them bring me to thy holy hill, and to thy tabernacles.

familiar.text: O send out thy light and thy truth: let them lead me; let them bring me unto thy holy hill, and to thy tabernacles.

modern.text: Send out Your light and Your truth; let them lead me. Let them bring me to Your holy mountain, and to the place where You dwell.

original.text: שְׁלַח אוֹרְךָ֣ וַ֭אֲמִתְּךָ הֵ֣מָּה יַנְח֑וּנִי יְבִיא֥וּנִי אֶל הַֽר קָ֝דְשְׁךָ֗ וְאֶל מִשְׁכְּנוֹתֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Then will I go to the altar of God, to God my exceeding joy: yea, upon the harp will I praise thee, O God my God.

familiar.text: Then will I go unto the altar of God, unto God my exceeding joy: yea, upon the harp will I praise thee, O God my God.

modern.text: Then I will go to the altar of God, to God, my greatest joy. I will praise You with the harp, O God, my God.

original.text: וְאָב֤וֹאָה אֶל מִזְבַּ֬ח אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֶל אֵל֮ שִׂמְחַ֪ת גִּ֫ילִ֥י וְאוֹדְךָ֥ בְכִנּ֗וֹר אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֱלֹהָֽי

verses.restored: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.

familiar.text: Why art thou cast down, O my soul? and why art thou disquieted within me? hope in God: for I shall yet praise him, who is the health of my countenance, and my God.

modern.text: Why are you downcast, O my soul? Why the unease within me? Put your hope in God, for I will yet praise Him, my Savior and my God.

original.text: מַה תִּשְׁתּ֬וֹחֲחִ֨י נַפְשִׁי֮ וּֽמַה תֶּהֱמִ֪י עָ֫לָ֥י הוֹחִ֣ילִי לֵֽ֭אלֹהִים כִּי ע֣וֹד אוֹדֶ֑נּוּ יְשׁוּעֹ֥ת פָּ֝נַ֗י וֵֽאלֹהָֽי

translation_notes: This chapter completes corpus coverage as a ChatGPT-authored draft. KJV is retained as a familiar comparison layer; a separate automated reference pass adds BSB and pointed Hebrew without replacing the restored draft.
safety_note: Enemy language remains poetic and cannot justify harm.
source_witness_audit_flags: Compare directly with WLC/OSHB, Septuagint, Dead Sea Psalms witnesses where extant, and other textual witnesses during the global audit. Preserve poetic parallelism, superscriptions, duplicate/parallel psalms, and significant Hebrew/Greek divergences rather than harmonizing them.
